post.description:
Create account.

create account (v1 legacy).
.5: holder callers can only create accounts owned by
themselves. Server-side defence-in-depth:
- If the caller is a holder (§4.3c — no `holder:view-all` scope) and
they did not supply `customer_id`, we resolve it from their Auth
user id (via `customers`).
- If the caller is a holder and they did supply a `customer_id` that
does not match their own, we return 403 (they cannot create
accounts for someone else).
- If no `customers` row exists for the holder, we return 403
— there is no way to own the account, so creating it would leave an
orphan (the list/get handlers then hide it forever).
- Callers with `holder:view-all` (staff / sys / M2M) are
unrestricted: they can pass any `customer_id` or none (for
internal accounts).

post.description:
Func host.

Sentin8:Func proxy-back for host functions.
Authorization: M2M token with `bank8:ledger:postings:write` (the Func
runtime authenticates with the posting service's M2M identity because
host functions can move money). Tenant context comes from the `env_id`
in the request body — the Func runtime resolves it from the hook
context, and the M2M token's own env claim is cross-checked.

Internal schedule run.

Cron proxy-back endpoint.
Cron calls this when a Ledger schedule fires. Ledger executes the scheduled
work (§4.3): it resolves the schedule's `schedule_type`, loads the affected
account(s) with their product modules + parameters, runs the on-schedule
module functions to generate posting instructions, and submits them as one
atomic posting batch. A `bank8_ledger_jobs` row records the outcome
`failed` + `error_message` when any step fails (never unconditionally
completed); `last_run_at` is updated only via propagated, awaited writes.

Authorization mirrors the platform's canonical Flow proxy-back gate
(sys `flow_delegate::execute_step`): the caller must present an
Auth-issued M2M bearer with `sentin8:sys:steps:execute` (Flow's
`sentin8-flow-sys` client). Transport identity (PQ-TLS + platform CA)
is machine identity, not service authorization; anonymous → 401,
wrong scope → 403. The workflow's env is cross-checked against the
bearer's env claim (a proxy-back can only act on an env its token
can address; the platform plane bypasses via `is_platform_admin`).

Flow proxy-back for the
`statement-regen` workflow (design §10).

Results are served from a bounded TTL cache (design §10): the
parameter-value write path is insert-only with `effective_from`, so a
short TTL self-heals and no event-driven invalidation is needed. The
posting money path never consults this cache — parameter resolution
there is transactional by design (a stale fee rate is a correctness
defect, not a latency trade).

ListAccountsQuery.description:
`GET /v1/accounts` — list accounts.
.5: holder callers (§4.3c — no `holder:view-all` scope) see only
accounts held by their own `customers` row, and only
`account_type='customer'` accounts (internal accounts are never exposed
to holders — forced here in the service layer; RLS is the backstop).
Callers with `holder:view-all` see all env accounts. A holder caller's
`?customer_id=` query param is ignored — they cannot impersonate another
customer.

env_id.description:
§10.1 — staff-realm env override for internal-account reads.
Validated against org membership; ignored for customer/delegated
tokens (env-locked) and never widens customer-data visibility.

Target env_id for the query. Staff tokens carry
env_id = System Env; the caller passes the real env_id here so
the query scopes to the correct environment. Ignored for
holder tokens (they are already env-scoped).

search.description: Free-text search: matches display_name or email (case-insensitive).

account.description: Synthetic account state — no persistence occurs.

hook.description: Hook name (pre_posting, post_posting, scheduled_event, activation, deactivation).

module_id.description: Func module id (the hook logic to execute).
